correctness.rationale: The published signed-filter definition reduces on a chain to one positive suffix point and one negative-minimal suffix point for each suffix; midpoint identities reduce the convex hull to an explicit simplex. Direct substitution proves the complete facet system and a positive linear dependence of its normals. Tangency equations plus that dependence give the exact inradius and unique incenter. Perpendicular-bisector recurrences give the displayed common vertex sphere. Its center lies in the ordinary order polytope, hence in the enriched order polytope, and a convex-contact parallel-axis identity proves that this sphere is the unique minimum enclosing sphere.

value.rationale: Enriched order polytopes are canonical reflexive poset polytopes, and the chain case gives a natural all-dimensional reflexive simplex family. The theorem determines both fundamental Euclidean ball radii, both centers, and their asymptotic aspect ratio. It also quantifies a genuine geometric distinction hidden by the published Ehrhart equivalence: for the same chain, the enriched chain partner is a crosspolytope with radius ratio only of order square-root dimension, while the enriched-order simplex has ratio of order dimension to the three-halves.
